key_insight: Adaptive reinforcement-learning attackers can learn to eavesdrop on BB84 far more stealthily than fixed-rate analytic attacks, sharply reducing detection while still extracting key information.
engineering_relevance: Quantum key distribution security evaluations should include adaptive adversary baselines, since learned attack policies can expose vulnerabilities in monitoring and checkpoint design.
method: Modeled Eve’s choice to intercept or pass each qubit as an MDP using QBER feedback.
Trained tabular Q-Learning, SARSA, and Double Q-Learning agents across three channel-noise levels.
Compared learned policies against a non-adaptive analytical baseline over 45 runs per condition and 10,000 episodes each.
evidence_signal: At 1% channel noise, Q-Learning reduced detection from 99.4% to 0.28% ± 0.27% while extracting about 10.5 correct bits per episode, with a statistically significant improvement (p=0.020).
watch_item: The reported stealth advantage can disappear when checkpoint intervals are randomized, so deployment assumptions and monitoring schedules matter.
paper_title: Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Eavesdropping in BB84 Quantum Key Distribution
